# PR description (draft)

Add 10 sk-cbor unit tests: `u64::MAX` decoding, nesting limits through the public `read`, `write`, `read_nested` and `write_nested` functions, and value ordering. Library code and existing tests are unchanged.

`test_read_unsigned_max` adds the RFC 8949 Appendix A `u64::MAX` case alongside `test_read_unsigned`, whose cases stop at `i64::MAX`.

The default-limit tests check the documented limit of 127 on `read` and `write`: 127 nested arrays pass and 128 fail with `TooMuchNesting`.

With `None`, `read_nested` decodes 128 nested arrays to the expected value and `write_nested` encodes them to the expected bytes. 128 is one level more than any `Some` limit allows (`i8::MAX` = 127). This follows #373, which keeps `None` as the way to skip the nesting check.

Existing tests already cover the limit logic: `test_read_too_much_nesting_error`, `test_write_single_levels`, `test_write_nested_map_levels`, `test_write_unbalanced_nested_containers` and `test_write_overly_nested`. These exercise the crate-private `Reader` and `Writer`; `test_write_nested_map_levels` and `test_write_overly_nested` already check successful writes with `None`.

The ordering tests complement `test_value_ordering` with equal-length arrays and maps whose first element or pair matches, and tags with the same tag number but different contents.

One open point: the tag tests check that `Some(0)` rejects and `Some(1)` accepts a tag that contains an integer. This pins that a tag uses one nesting level, as the code does now; the docs do not say so. Please confirm, or the two tag tests can be dropped.
